bounded_claim: Two adjacent Invalid diagnostic lines are source-explained nested rejection messages for one recorded DDR guest fault. The0x1c line does not establish a second guest instruction or a guest physical read of address0x1c. An earlier, different Data Abort remains recorded separately; no only-one-abort-in-the-entire-run claim is made. No offset value, DDR payload access, or firmware runtime producer state is inferred.
explanation: The board maps only the4B RPM offset region at physical0x0c3f0004. flatview_add_to_dispatch/register_subpage create a subpage wrapper for the surrounding page; its other bytes remain unassigned.
The CPU IOTLB path calls address_space_translate_internal with resolve_subpage=false. The outer access is therefore expressed at wrapper offset0x1c, while subpage_accepts adds page base0x0c3f0000.
subpage_accepts calls flatview_access_valid at physical0x0c3f001c. The inner unassigned_mem_accepts returns false, and inner memory_region_access_valid emits the full-address rejection.

The false result propagates back to outer memory_region_access_valid for the subpage wrapper, which emits the second rejection using offset0x1c. Both wrappers have NULL region names in these diagnostics.

The outer memory_region_dispatch_read returns MEMTX_DECODE_ERROR. The captured trace then records one corresponding DDR Data Abort, whose ELR/FAR match the printk PC/X0. The observed ordering is explained by nested validity checks for the same recorded faulting32-bit guest load.
